area: transform/UnCurry (try lifting) and Erasure (value class boxing)
title: A try in a guarded match that is the body of a partial function with a value class result fails verification (VerifyError; AnalyzerException under -opt:local)
oracle: -opt:local against the reference (crash); the reference itself fails verification when the method runs
generator: wave4/harness/programs/Gen.scala, round-4 grammar: partial function literal of a value class type, Int switch with a constant guard and a try/catch arm
detail: ({ case x => x match { case 100 if false => V0(1.0); case 3 => try V0(0.5) catch { case _: Exception => V0(0.6) }; case _ => V0(3.0) } }: PartialFunction[Int, V0]).applyOrElse(i, ...) with V0 a value class compiles, but the anonymous function class fails verification when it is loaded (Inconsistent stackmap frames), and with -opt:local the compiler crashes with AnalyzerException 'Incompatible stack heights' in the call-graph type analysis of applyOrElse. UnCurry leaves the try in place because, as a case body, it is evaluated on an empty operand stack. applyOrElse returns the erased result type Object, so erasure boxes the value class around the whole translated match: the posterasure tree is matchEnd3(new V0({ ...case7(){ if (3 == x1) matchEnd5(try 0.5 catch ...) ... } })), and the try now runs with the NEW and DUP of the box on the stack, which a handler entry clears. Without the constant-false guard, without the value class (Double), or outside a partial function (a generic method with the same body), it works. It is the CF3 family (a try that a later phase puts behind a non-empty stack); retronym/scala#605 handles receivers rewritten by erasure, not value-class boxing. Ordinary code reaches it rarely: it needs a partial function (collect, applyOrElse, recover) producing a value class, and a match that patmat does not turn into a switch.
fix_sketch: Box a value class result arm by arm (push the box into the match end label's argument) rather than around the whole block, or have UnCurry lift a try whose enclosing expression has a value-class type in a position erasure will box. No binary compatibility cost.
prior: CF3 / retronym/scala#605 (same family, different trigger); scala/bug#9390 for try lifting in constructors; none found for value-class boxing
